target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K → Def3 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ)) →
    𝓢 ⊢ ⊥
a_raw: {"translation": "Target is the proposition asserting that for every type Fm of sentences equipped with the internal connectives implication (🡒), conjunction (⋏), disjunction (⋎), negation (∼) (with biconditional φ 🡘 ψ abbreviating (φ 🡒 ψ) ⋏ (ψ 🡒 φ)) and constants truth (⊤) and falsehood (⊥); for every pair of types S₀ and S of proof systems equipped with provability relations on Fm; for every proof system 𝓑 of type S₀ and every proof system 𝓢 of type S such that both 𝓑 and 𝓢 prove all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and are closed under modus ponens; and for every pair of arbitrary functions K and F from Fm to Fm: if all seven of the following hypotheses hold—(1) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓑 proves K φ; (2) every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (3) for all sentences φ and ψ, 𝓢 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ); (4) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves (K φ) 🡒 φ; (5) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡒 φ); (6) there exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ); and (7) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡘 (F φ))—then 𝓢 proves ⊥ (falsehood). Nothing else is assumed: K and F are arbitrary functions on sentences with no syntactic or arithmetic structure; neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is assumed consistent; the necessitation rule in (1) is assumed only for 𝓑 (not for 𝓢); hypotheses (3), (4), (5), and (7) are assumed only for 𝓢 (not for 𝓑); hypothesis (6) requires only a single sentence ψ provably equivalent in 𝓑 to ∼(F ψ); and the conclusion is specifically that 𝓢 proves ⊥ (not that 𝓑 proves ⊥)."}
translation: Target is the proposition asserting that for every type Fm of sentences equipped with the internal connectives implication (🡒), conjunction (⋏), disjunction (⋎), negation (∼) (with biconditional φ 🡘 ψ abbreviating (φ 🡒 ψ) ⋏ (ψ 🡒 φ)) and constants truth (⊤) and falsehood (⊥); for every pair of types S₀ and S of proof systems equipped with provability relations on Fm; for every proof system 𝓑 of type S₀ and every proof system 𝓢 of type S such that both 𝓑 and 𝓢 prove all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and are closed under modus ponens; and for every pair of arbitrary functions K and F from Fm to Fm: if all seven of the following hypotheses hold—(1) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓑 proves K φ; (2) every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (3) for all sentences φ and ψ, 𝓢 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ); (4) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves (K φ) 🡒 φ; (5) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡒 φ); (6) there exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ); and (7) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡘 (F φ))—then 𝓢 proves ⊥ (falsehood). Nothing else is assumed: K and F are arbitrary functions on sentences with no syntactic or arithmetic structure; neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is assumed consistent; the necessitation rule in (1) is assumed only for 𝓑 (not for 𝓢); hypotheses (3), (4), (5), and (7) are assumed only for 𝓢 (not for 𝓑); hypothesis (6) requires only a single sentence ψ provably equivalent in 𝓑 to ∼(F ψ); and the conclusion is specifically that 𝓢 proves ⊥ (not that 𝓑 proves ⊥).

divergences.description: Omission of the object-language existential quantifier ∃e in SSMT (∃e K(K = F_e)). Koellner's Theorem 6 asserts that EA_T + ∃e K(K = F_e) is inconsistent, whereas Target cannot express object-language quantifiers and instead quantifies externally (at the meta-level) over a fixed function F. Proving inconsistency for each externally fixed F is strictly weaker than proving EA_T + ∃e K(K = F_e) inconsistent, since it does not formalize the refutation uniformly inside the theory over the variable e and therefore does not rule out nonstandard witnesses e.

Omission of arithmetic, Gödel numbering, Turing machines (F_e / W_m), and the base theory EA_T, with the existence of a Gödel sentence assumed as an abstract hypothesis (Def5 𝓑 F). In Koellner's Theorem 6 (and Alexander's passages), the theorem concerns Epistemic Arithmetic and Turing machines/r.e. predicates applied to Gödel numbers ⌜φ⌝, where the diagonal lemma for every F_e is an arithmetical theorem. Target instead quantifies over an arbitrary classical propositional type Fm and arbitrary functions K, F : Fm → Fm, assuming ∃ ψ, 𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼F ψ as a hypothesis; it thus formalizes an abstract propositional modal impossibility lemma rather than a theorem about EA_T and Turing machines.

Replacement of the single object-language sentence K(K = F_e) (which requires the truth predicate of EA_T and universal quantification over sentences inside the scope of K) by the meta-level schema ∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ). While Target cannot express EA_T's truth predicate or the single sentence K(K = F_e), for a fixed F deriving inconsistency from the sentence-by-sentence schema uses a weaker hypothesis (strengthening the fixed-F result) and mirrors the schema form of Alexander's Theorem 12 (with F φ in place of ⌜φ⌝ ∈ W_m).

Weakening of the epistemic and logical background axioms via the two-system split 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢. Rather than full EA/EA_T (which includes S4 positive introspection Kφ → KKφ, necessitation for the whole theory, first-order logic, Peano arithmetic, and truth axioms), Target assumes only classical propositional logic for 𝓑 and 𝓢, necessitation (Def1) and a single diagonal sentence (Def5) for 𝓑, and K-distribution (Def2), factivity (Def3), and explicit known factivity (Def4) for 𝓢. Since these hypotheses are strictly weaker than EA_T (where known factivity follows from factivity and necessitation), this is a harmless strengthening that also isolates the role of known factivity emphasized by Alexander.

judgement.summary: Target is a sound abstract propositional modal inconsistency lemma using the sentence-by-sentence schema of Alexander's Theorem 12 and explicit known factivity, but it diverges majorly from Koellner's Theorem 6 because it omits EA_T, arithmetic, Gödel numbering, Turing machines, and the object-language existential quantifier ∃e of SSMT, assuming a diagonal sentence for an externally fixed arbitrary operator F instead.
